Chapter 10. The Enduring Power of Persistence: Reflections on Service and Change
Every now and then, when things got quiet—when the cameras were off, the crowds had faded, and the day’s noise had settled—Nancy would find herself drifting back in time.
She’d remember that crowded living room in Baltimore, the warm lessons from her parents, and the long, winding road that eventually brought her right to the center of American power.
That journey? It was so much tougher—and so much longer—than she could’ve ever pictured. There were moments of real triumph, but also heartbreak, victories mixed with tough losses.
One thing Nancy always understood: the work was never truly finished. Every generation gets its own set of challenges, its own moments of crisis and big opportunities. The specific issues change, the faces at the table change, but there’s always that need for steady, principled leadership.
For her, the biggest lesson was actually pretty simple—persistence is what counts.
Showing up, day in and day out. Doing the hard work, even when nobody’s watching. That’s what really makes the difference. She’d seen, time and again, how small acts of kindness could ripple out in ways you’d never expect. How quiet determination could move actual mountains. And how just one person’s courage to stand alone could inspire others to step up and join them.
Most people think history is shaped by these huge, dramatic gestures, right? But Nancy saw it differently. She knew the real change—lasting change—happened in the everyday grind. The phone calls, the meetings, the quiet, thoughtful conversations. All those little moments add up, and over time, they build something that lasts.
Looking back over her career, Nancy felt this deep gratitude. For every person who supported her, for each chance she got to serve, and for the opportunity to make even a small difference.
She understood that the work wouldn’t end with her. It’d be carried forward by new voices, fresh ideas, and that same spirit of service that lit her path from the very beginning.
